[THREAD🧵]  The Indian general elections are going to be held from April 2024 and the results will be declared in June 2024. Since independence, the elections will be held in a situation where two chief ministers are incarcerated, the bank a/c of the largest opposition party is frozen, ...(1)

... raids of IT, CBI, and ED (investigation agencies) on opposition leaders are at a rampant level, unelected governors are in a position where they're stifling elected parties from ruling their states, the finances of southern states are being controlled by the Union government,... (2)

... islamophobia is at its peak and many more things.   We didn't reach at this point in our "electoral democracy" all of a sudden. Rather these tendencies have been there for thousands of years; the urge to monopolise power. Since independence, despite getting a progressive constitution, ... (3)

this tendency has been part and parcel of Indian democracy. The incumbent govt has used state institutions to crack down on opposition politicians but even then, there was a consciousness among the power holders of power being fleeting, no matter how long you hold the power. (4)

Apart from the fleeting nature of the power, there was also this consciousness of distribution of power, although, this was involuntary and was an outcome of diminishing monopoly of Congress in some areas, maturing electoral democracy and the need to accommodate a range of voices. (5)

I believe these are some of the normal conditions to preserve the functioning of the parliamentary system.   In contrast to the situation mentioned above, today, we're at a phase in our "electoral democracy" where the incumbent doesn't believe in the above-stated fundamentals. The BJP, riding... (6)

... on Hindutva wave, masked by anti-corruption pledges and the need for a strong leader stormed to power with an overwhelming majority. They promised all sorts of services and amenities. They vowed to cleanse the politics of corruption and black money. (7)

In this CASI Deep Dive INDIA IN TRANSITION Interview, CASI Managing Editor @rohanvenkat.bsky.social speaks to author Eswaran Sridharan (UPIASI) about "the 2024 Elections and India’s Unique Coalition Politics" casi.sas.upenn.edu/iit/rohan-ve...

E. Sridharan’s book “Elections, Parties, and Coalitions in India: Theory and Recent History” presents 10 papers on India’s history with coalition politics, how parties have used and been affected by coalitional strategies, and India’s party system compared to other democracies.
E. Sridharan has closely followed India’s political developments over the years, and most recently published an EPW paper examining pre-electoral coalition politics in the 2024 general elections.

CASI Managing Editor @rohanvenkat.bsky.social spoke to E. Sridharan about the results of the 2024 general elections, the “beginnings of a loose bipolarity” between two big national blocks in India’s Parliament…
…and how the strategies used in pre-electoral coalitions make India rather unique and particularly different from the European nations that form the bulk of coalition literature in political science.
